chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, who said:

I saw Abdullah ibn Jundub at the Mawqif (Station), and I did not see a station that was better than his station. He continued extending his hands to the sky, and his tears were flowing upon his cheeks until they reached the ground. So when the people left, I said to him, 'O Abu Muhammad! I have not seen a station at all that was better than your station.' He said, 'By Allah, I did not supplicate except for my brethren. And that is because Abu Al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) informed me that whoever supplicates for his brother in his absence, a call is made from the Throne, and for you is a hundred thousand times the like of it. Therefore, I disliked that I should leave a guaranteed hundred thousand times for one person, whom I do not know if he will be answered for or not.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The Station (Mawqif), specifically referring to the place of standing during Hajj, often Arafat
key_terms.بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ: In his absence / behind his back

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for supplicating for a brother in his absence according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual etiquette of the Mawqif at Arafat, where Abdullah ibn Jundub prioritized intercessory supplication for others based on the teaching of Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS). The Imam’s report of a 'guaranteed' reward of one hundred thousand times the merit underscores the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity and the efficacy of du'a for the absent, contrasting it with the uncertainty of personal rewards. This practice reflects the broader theological principle that seeking forgiveness and blessings for the community is a means of securing divine favor.
